# Negative-result handoff

State the frozen question, primary criteria and observed outcome first. Identify the input/code evidence and its limits. Record failed hypotheses, non-admitted ideas, costs and selection effects without retrospectively changing the decision rule.

Separate descriptive diagnostics from the primary verdict. Explain what the result does and does not establish. Keep any future sensitivity analysis distinct, with its own authority, trial accounting and disclosure. An unfavorable result does not create an obligation to keep searching.

Record the stopping decision and specific new evidence that could justify future independent work. Preserve the original record; do not replace it with a more flattering rerun.
